caseno:
Writ Petition No. 911 of 2002 
with 
Writ Petition 1454 of 1994
lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam with Probir Neogi, Advocates - For the Petitioners (In both the Writ Petitions)
Rajik-Al-Jalil, Assistant-Attorney-General -For Respondent No. 2 in WP 911 of 2002. For Respondent No.1 in WP 1454 of 1994. 
SS Halder, Advocate -For the added Respondents Nos. 3 and 4 in WP 1454 of 1994.
parties:
Asaf Khan and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Court of Settlement, First Court & others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
3. In Writ Petition 1454 of 1994, a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to give effect to the Memo No. Sha 12/1 R-4/83/104(3) dated 10-4-85 of the Secretary, Ministry of Works, Government of Bangladesh (Annexure-A1) and the resolution of the Abandoned Properties Disposal and Management Board, Dhaka City (respondent No. 2) as taken in the meeting dated 17-12-92 and communicated to the petitioner No.1 under Memo No. APMB-7/93-20 /2 (II) dated 6-3-93 (Annexure-F) and register the ¾ th portion of the property of 58/1, Purana Paltan, PS Motijheel, Dhaka to the petitioners within a specified period of time on receipt of Taka 26,34,187.50/- and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. The case of the petitioners, inter alia, is that they are occupying and running their business in the case holding No. 58/1 Purana Paltan, Dhaka. The case property belonged to one Mahmuda Khatun, wife of Mr. Khawaja Golam Hossain. The property was initially khas mahal land of the Government and by successive transfer the wife of Khawja Golam Hossain acquired ownership of the property comprising 10 kathas of land. Subsequently a portion was acquired by the Government for construction of road and balance remained 6 kathas of land on which an old dilapidated 3 storied building was situated. Mahmuda Khatun died in 1959. Khawaja Golam Hossain was a government servant and he retired in 1972 as Deputy Director of Bangladesh Fire Services. The case property was declared as abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972. But on the application of Khawaja Golam Hossain the case property was released from the list of abandoned properties by memo dated 29-10-1974. Khawaja Golam Hossain claimed the entire case property as his property by virtue of inheritance from his wife and he mutated his name in the government revenue records, paid all rents and taxes in respect of the case property, used to collect rent from the tenants of the case property including the present petitioners. 

 6. Khawaja Golam Hossain offered to sell the case property and the petitioners believing him to be the sole owner of the case property agreed to purchase it and as a result the petitioners purchased the entire case property by five registered deeds dated 26-2-1982 for a total consideration of Taka 7 lacs. The petitioners also paid Taka 1,75,000/- to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka as transfer fee, the holding being Khas Mahal property and paid Taka 1,53,770/- as ground rents, municipal taxes in respect of entire holding until 1994. Subsequently it was discovered that Khawja Golam Hossain's wife died leaving behind not only Khawja Golam Hossain as her husband but also some children and Khawja Golam Hossain became the owner of ¼ th share of the case property. It was found that the children of Mahmuda Khatun were living in Pakistan at the time of Liberation War and consequently, ¾ th share of the case property vested in the Government as abandoned property. The Ministry of Works made thorough investigation into the ownership of the case property and on obtaining opinion of the Ministry of Law in this regard, the Government in the Ministry of Works by a Memo dated 22-4-1984 informed petitioner No.1 that 3/4th of the case property is abandoned and 1/4th of the case property will be deemed to have been released and accordingly, the memo dated 29-10-1974 was modified. 

 7. In this situation the petitioners offered to purchase the ¼th share of the case property from the Government and after continued negotiations the Government agreed to sell 3/4th share of the property to the petitioners, assessed the value of the case property at Taka 35,12,250/- and informed petitioner No.1 portion of the case property to the petitioners at Taka 26,34,187/50 (being the price stipulated period. In the said writ petition the Secretary to Government in the Ministry of Works was impleaded as respondent No.1 and the present petitioners were impleaded as respondents Nos. 4-8. Both the Government and the present petitioners filed separate affidavits-in-opposition contesting the Rule. Ultimately, upon hearing the parties, a Division Bench of this Court discharged the Rule by judgment and order dated 28-5-1991. In the judgment of Writ Petition 57 of 1985 the holding number of the property was written as 59,K/1 Purana Paltan instead of 58/1, Purana Paltan. This Court by an order dated 14-11-1991 corrected the mistake. It is borne out from the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Government, Annexure-F, in WP No. 57 of 1985 that the Government came out with the case that the petitioners are owners of ¼ th portion of the case property by virtue of purchase from Khawaja Golam Hossain and only ¾ th portion of the case property was abandoned property. After disposal of the above writ petition the petitioners by their letters dated 17-12-1991 and 10-12-1991 informed the Secretary of the Ministry about the result of the writ petition and requested him for direction as to 3/4th portion of the case property by memo dated 10-4-1985 wherein the Government asked the petitioners to pay the price of 3/4th portion of the case property to the Executive Engineer, Abandoned Houses, Segun Bagicha, Dhaka within 15 days of the receipt of the memo. 

 8. The petitioners were ready and willing to deposit the money for purchase of the property but on 13-4-85 a writ petition No. 57 of 1985 was filed by Atahar Mollah and Seraj Mia who were occupying one semi pucca tin-shed and a portion of the ground floor of the disputed holding. The semi pucca constructions were without any sanction of Dhaka Improvement Trust, (now RAJUK) They, however, were paying rent to Khawja Golam Hossain. A Division Bench of this Court issued Rule Nisi on 15-4-1985 upon the Government and also on the present petitioners to show cause why the memo dated 10-4-1985 would not be declared to be without lawful authority and pending hearing, of the Rule stayed the operation of the said impugned memo dated 10-4-1985. s a result the petitioners could not make payment of the price for 3/4th portion of the case property to the Government within the stipulated period. In the said writ petition the Secretary to Government in the Ministry of Works was impleaded as respondent No.1 and the present petitioners were impleaded as respondent Nos. 4-8. Both the Government and the present petitioners filed separate affidavits-in-opposition contesting the Rule. Ultimately, upon hearing the parties, a Division Bench of this Court discharged the Rule by judgment and order dated 28-5-1991. In the judgment of Writ Petition 57 of 1985 the holding number of the property was written as 59,k/1 Purana Paltan instead of 58/1, Purana Paltan. This Court by an order dated 14-11-1991 corrected the mistake. It is borne out from the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Government, Annexure-F, in WP No. 57/1985 that the Government came out with the case that the petitioners are owners of 3/4th portion of the case property by virtue of purchase from Khawaja Golam Hossain and only 3/4th portion of the case property was abandoned property. After disposal of the above writ petition the petitioners by their letters dated 7-12-1991 and 10-12-1991 informed the Secretary of the Ministry about the result of the writ petition and requested him for direction as to how and under what head the money is to be deposited. In the meantime the question of dealing with the disposal and management of abandoned properties in the city of Dhaka was entrusted to Abandoned Property Disposal and Management Board, and the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, was designated as its Chairman. Accordingly the said Board by the resolution in a meeting held on 17-12-1992 confirmed the decision to sell the 3/4th portion of the property to the petitioners with the said offered price. A copy of the said decision was sent to petitioner No.1 on 6-3-1993. In response, the petitioners by their letter dated 6-6-1993 requested the Chairman of the Board for direction as to whom the sum of Taka 26,34,187/50 is to be deposited and also requested him to make early settlement of the other matters of the case property. Without getting any further response, petitioner No.1 approached the Chairman of the Board times without number for implementation of decision of the Board and for registration of the property in favour of the petitioners. Every time the Chairman was giving assurance that the Board was pledged bound by its resolution and promise of the Government in the Ministry of Works and the resolution would be implemented definitely as soon as possible. Ultimately, without getting any effective result from the Board the petitioner No.1 on behalf of all the petitioners addressed a letter to the Minister-in-Charge of Ministry of Works on 28-4-1994 with a copy to the Chairman of the Board requesting implementation of the resolution of the Board and also the earlier decision of the Ministry on the Memo dated 10-4-1985 for transfer of the property i.e. 3/4th portion of holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan to the petitioners on receipt of the consideration money. But as there was no response from the Government, the petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 before this Court for a direction to give effect of the Memo dated 10-4-1985 and resolution dated 17-12-1992 of the Abandoned Property Management Board and obtained a Rule on the respondents on 20-9-1994. 

 13. The Government being respondent No. 2 in Writ Petition No. 911 of 2002 and respondent No.1 in Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 contested both the Rules by filing two affidavits-in-opposition and denied the material allegations made in the writ petition. Delco Engineering represented by Atahar Mollah and Al-Basking Tailors Private Ltd represented by Firoz Miah by filing separate affidavits-in-opposition contested the Rule in Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 as added respondent Nos. 3-4 denying the material allegations made in the writ petition. The case of the respondent-government in Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 is almost the same as in Writ Petition No. 911 of 2002. 

 14. It is stated by the respondent-Government that the case property is in possession of the Government by collecting rent from the tenants. It is further stated that Mahmuda Khatun, wife of Khawja Golam Hossain was the owner of the disputed holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, she died in 1959 leaving her husband Khawja Golam Hossain, 5 sons namely, (1) Salauddin, (2) Shahabuddin, (3) Shami, (4) Nami, (5) Seraj And 4 daughters namely, (1) Zarina, (2) Nasrin, (3) Jafrin and (4) Shirin and accordingly, they inherited the disputed property. The sons and daughters of Mahmuda Khatun became the owners to the extent of 3/4th share while her husband got 1/4th share. It is also stated that during liberation war, the husband, sons and daughters of Mahmuda Khatun left this country and permanently settled in Pakistan and as their whereabouts were not known the disputed property was declared abandoned property and vested in the Government by operation of law. Thereafter one Khawja Golam Hossain claiming himself as husband of Mahmuda Khatun made a representation to the Government on 14-3-1974 praying for dropping the disputed property from the list of the abandoned properties. Khawja Golam Hossain in his representation stated that his sons and daughters were minors and were living under his care and custody. Though the property was treated as abandoned property under President's Order 16 of 1972 but, on good faith, relying on the statements contained in the representation dated 14-3-1974 of Khawja Golam Hossain the Government dropped the disputed property from the list of the Abandoned Properties vide memo dated 29-10-1974. Subsequently, it was found that the sons and daughters of Mahmuda Khatun had been living in Pakistan since the emergence of Bangladesh and are not the residents of Bangladesh and they were Pakistani citizens but Khawaja Golam Hossain in his representation dated 14-3-1974, upon which the disputed property was dropped from the list of abandoned property, concealed this. As such, the Government vide memo dated 22-4-1984 amended the earlier order dated 29-10-1974 by which 3/4th share of Mahmuda Khatun's sons and daughters in the disputed property remained abandoned and 1/4th of the case property would be deemed to have been released. Thereafter as there were symptoms of fraudulent activities to grab the case property by Khawja Golam Hossain a question has also been raised as to whether Khawja Golam Hossain who claimed to be the husband of Mahmuda Khatun is her real husband or not. In that view of the matter the Government treated whole of the disputed property as abandoned property and listed in the Ka list as per Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. In the meantime the Government knew that Khawja Golam Hossain had been trying to dispose of the property but he could not get any scope to dispose of the entire property at all when heirs of Mahmuda Khatun are Pakistani nationals. Thereafter, it was informed to the Government that concealing the real fact about the property and showing him as the sole owner of the property Khawja Golam Hossain, in collusion with the petitioners, transferred whole of the property including the share of the Pakistani nationals by 5 separate registered deeds without depositing transfer fee to the Government and KG Hossain managed to leave the country for Pakistan with the sale proceeds and this fraudulent transaction cannot be said to have been validly done. 

 15. In this situation the petitioners offered to purchase the 3/4th share of the case property from the Government. The Government in good faith agreed to sell 3/4th share of the case property to the petitioners at Taka 26,34,187.50/- and informed the petitioner No.1 accordingly by memo dated 10-4-1985 to pay the price of 3/4th portion of the case property to the Executive Engineer, Abandoned Houses Circle, Shegunbagicha, within 15 days of the receipt of the memo. The petitioners, however, did not pay the above amount within 15 days of the receipt of the Memo dated 10-4-1985 nor as yet. Though the Abandoned Property Disposal and Management Board, in its meeting on 17-12-1992, took a decision to sell the property to the petitioners in terms and conditions of the earlier memo dated 10-4-1985, but the petitioners did not comply with the decision of the Government. 

 16. It is also stated that Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 filed by Atahar Mollah and Seraj Mia challenging the Ministry's above mentioned letter dated 10-4-1985 was ultimately disposed of on 28-5-1991 and the Rule was discharged. It is further stated that without having proper scope to scrutinise the Government admitted only 3/4th portion of the case property as abandoned in their earlier affidavit-in-opposition in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985. It was found, thereafter, that entire case property was listed as abandoned property on 23-9-1986 and, as such, the petitioners could not be treated as the owner of 1/4th portion property of the case property. Not only that, it was also asserted by some other persons that the sale deeds of the petitioners regarding the case property were not executed by the proper person. In this situation the concerned Ministry by their letter dated 10-12-1994 requested the petitioners to submit sale deeds in their favour to the Ministry for proper scrutiny. In reply the petitioners vide their letter dated 24-12-1994 refused to submit the sale deeds on the ground of pendency of Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 before this court. 

 17. It is further submitted by the respondent-Government that the petitioners were required to prove that Khawaja Golam Hossain is the husband of Mahmuda Khatun and he himself sold out the case property to them by registered deeds. Then only they could claim ¼ th of the case property to be not treated as abandoned property but the petitioners could not prove their case before the Court of Settlement; the Court of Settlement after examination of the documents as well as oral evidence rightly dismissed the case of the petitioners and maintained enlistment of the entire property in Ka list. 

 18. The petitioners by filing affidavits-in-reply to the affidavits-in-opposition filed by the Government-respondent denied the material allegations made in the affidavits-in-opposition. In reply the petitioners stated that the Government made investigation into the matter and after taking opinion of the Ministry of Law released ¼ th share of the disputed property in favour of the petitioners. Hence it does not lie in the mouth of the respondent to say that the released portion of the disputed property is abandoned property. In this regard the petitioners stated that the Government filed affidavit in opposition in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 wherein it was admitted that ¼ th portion of the disputed property was not abandoned property and if the Government wants to contradict those statements, the Government is required to produce the relevant file to show what enquiry was made by the Government after making the statement in the aforesaid affidavit on the basis of which the contrary statement is made. The contrary statements made now in the affidavit-in-opposition are untrue and run counter to the official records. It is also stated that after purchase in 1982 by the petitioners, the Government in the Ministry of Works made thorough investigation and examined the kabalas executed by Khawja Golam Hossain which were produced by the petitioners and the notes 87 to 89 dated 26-6-1983 of the Government file run as follows: 

 "87. Now Mr. Asaf Khan has come with a petition claiming ownership of the property by virtue of deed of transfer by Khawja Golam Hossain. His petition and other papers in support of his claim may please to be seen at page 150/C, Khawja Golam Hossain got the property mutated in his name from ADC (Rev) on payment of usual fees under section 173 of GE Manual on 31-8-81. Subsequently, be sold the property to Mr. Asaf Khan and others on 26-2-82 by registered deed. On the basis of this sale deed, Asaf Khan and others got their names mutated vide page 125/Cor." 

 19. It is also stated that not only did the Ministry of Works examine the papers of the petitioners, they had the matter investigated by CID and after the investigation the matter was referred to the learned Attorney General who rendered opinion in the Government file and thereafter the Ministry of Works issued the Memo dated 22-4-1984. In this situation there was no question of examining the documents of the petitioners in December 1984, particularly when the matter was pending before this Court. Even then petitioner No.1 met the Secretary to the Ministry of Works in January, 1995 with the original kabalas and attested photocopies thereof. The Secretary to the Ministry of Works, examined the original kabalas and returned those to the petitioner No.1 keeping the attested photocopies thereof in the Government file. It is also stated that it had never been the case of the Government that Khawja Golam Hossain was not the husband of Mahmuda Khatun and the government after being satisfied about the status of Khawja Golam Hossain issued Memos dated 22-4-1984 and 10-4-1985. It is further stated that relying on the order of release passed by the Government and mutation of the name of Khawja Golam Hossain in the official record, the petitioners purchased the disputed property and, as such, the Government is estopped from denying the right of the petitioners. It is further submitted that after having released ¼th share of the disputed property from the list of the abandoned property the Government has no legal right to treat it as abandoned property and the present contention of the Government is illegal. It is reiterated that the petitioners Could not make the payment demanded by the memo dated 10-4-1985 within 15 days as in the meantime this Court on 15-4-1985 (before the expiry of 15 days) issued Rule in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 and stayed the operation of the aforesaid memo. It is further stated that Memo dated 10-4-1985 was not endorsed to the Executive Engineer who would not accept the money from the petitioners without any instruction. 

 20. The case of the added respondent Nos. 3-4 of Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 as stated in their affidavit-in-opposition and two other additional affidavits is that the said holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan consists of 4270 decimals of land in 2 plots namely, 1255 and 1269. The original owner Surobala Ghose took lease on 2-1-1943 from the Government by a deed of lease agreement and transferred the same to Loujee Curjsetjee in 1951 who in his turn transferred the same to Hussain Teja Bhaivimani in 1952. Hussain Teja Bhaivimani constructed a building to the western part of the said land. In 1955 Mahmuda Khatun, wife of Khawja Golam Hossain purchased the disputed holding. Mahmuda Khatun died in 1959 and upon her death her husband Khawja Golam Hossain, 5 sons and 4 daughters inherited her right, title and interest in the property. 

 22. The further case of the added respondent is that since the property was enlisted as abandoned property in Ka list, Khawja Golam Hossain had no authority to sell the same. Khawja Golam Hossain was owner of ¼th portion of the property but he sold the entire property and, as such, the transfer is not valid. As Mahmuda Khatun was the owner by purchase of the case property measuring 13.83 decimals of land and the ¼th share inherited by Khawja Golam Hossain comes to 3.46 decimals and more than his share was purchased by petitioner No.1, the four other petitioners cannot have any claim. The added respondents further stated that the malafide and improper transfer in favour of the petitioners by 5 registered deeds was made without permission of the Government and without depositing the necessary transfer fee as required for transfer of the khas mahal land and the subsequent deposit of Taka 1,75,000/- by the petitioner No.1, on the objection raised by the added respondents, does not cure the illegality of the transfer of the abandoned property in favour of the petitioners. 

 23. The further case of the added respondents is that there cannot be any commitment for sale of any portion of the property either by the Government or by the Divisional Commissioner as the property was finally published in Ka list of the abandoned property. The Divisional Commissioner has no jurisdiction to take any resolution relating to the disposal of abandoned property. 

 28. We have heard Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners and Mr. Rajik-Al-Jalil, the learned Assistant Attorney General for the Government in both writ petitions. We have also heard Mr SS Haider the learned Advocate for the added respondents in Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994. 

 29. In Writ Petition No. 911 of 2002 the legality of the judgment of the Court of Settlement has been challenged. The Court of Settlement refused to release 1/4th share of the holding in question from the list of Abandoned Properties in favour the petitioners. Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994 has been brought for a direction to give effect to the Memo dated 10-4-1985 of the Government and Resolution dated 17-12-1992 of the Abandoned Property Management Board to sell 3/4th share of the holding to the petitioners. From the contentions of the contesting parties it appears that if the petitioners succeed in the former Writ Petition then they can assert their right in the latter. 

 31. Mr. Mahmudul Islam submits that the government having been satisfied with the identity and status of Khawja Golam Hossain released the entire holding from the list of Abandoned Properties by memo dated 29-10-1974 [Annexure-B] and subsequently after thorough investigation by the memo dated 22-4-1984 [Annexure-D] modified the release order to the extent of ¼ th share of the holding and from this decision of the authority concerned it is clear that earlier release of the ¼ th share of the disputed property was upheld and maintained by the Government. He further submits that in the affidavit in opposition filed by the Government in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985, [Annexure-E] the Government also admitted that 1/4th share was released in favour of the Khawja Golam Hossain. In view of this position, Mr. Islam argued that the enlistment of 1/4th share of the petitioners in the disputed holding as Abandoned Property is without any basis. 

 32. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submits that the consistent case of the Government is that they released 1/4th share of the disputed property and the question raised by the Court of Settlement regarding genuineness of Khawja Golam Hossain and documents executed by Khawja Golam Hossain in favour of the petitioners were beyond the scope of the case filed under section 7 of the Ordinance 54 of 1985. Mr. Islam referred to the evidence of petitioner No.1 Asaf Khan before the Court of Settlement (Annexure-M) and submits that the present petitioner No.1 as PW 1 before the Court of Settlement was cross-examined but the genuineness of kabalas executed in their favour were not at all challenged. He also referred to list of documents filed before the Court of Settlement with First (Annexure-L) to show that the petitioners filed 5 registered kabalas executed in their favour by Khawja Golam Hossain. Mr. Islam also referred to a letter dated 6-1-1981 [Annexure-J] addressed by Khawja Golam Hossain, Retired Deputy Director, Fire Services, Government of Bangladesh to the Director of Fire Services, Government of Bangladesh to return his service book as the same was his personal property and the reply dated 22-1-1981 (Annexure-K) of the Director by which service book was returned to Khawja Golam Hossain on his request. From this learned Advocate argued that it is proved that Khawja Golam Hossain was in Bangladesh at least up to 1981. He also referred to the mutation order dated 31-8-1989 in Miscellaneous Case 74 of 1980 of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka (Annexure-B1) showing that the name of Khawja Golam Hossain was mutated in respect of the entire holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka under section 170B of Government Estate Manual on receipt of usual transfer fee. 

 33. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, therefore, submits that the preponderance of documents will go to show that the Court of Settlement did not at all consider the documents filed by the petitioners as provided under law which made the impugned judgment without jurisdiction. In support of his contention Mr. Islam has cited the case of Miah Jamal Shah vs Member, Election Commission, Government of Pakistan and others; reported in 18 DLR (SC) 1 wherein it has been observed that "so far administrative officer and authorities ate concerned there is no distinction between illegality and want of jurisdiction. When an administrative officer acts illegally he acts without jurisdiction. An administrative officer has authority to pass order or to take action if certain facts exist. If those essential facts do not exist his order or action is void." 

 34. Mr. Islam further contended that the Court of Settlement dismissed the case without considering material evidence which caused prejudice to the present petitioners. Mr. Islam further argued that the Court of Settlement arrived at a wrong decision in consideration of some extraneous matters which were beyond the scope and jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement in the matter like this. He then submits, that the High Court Division can interfere with the finding of a Tribunal of facts under its extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution when it could be shown that the Tribunal had acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence/facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or that it had acted malafide or in violation of any principle of natural justice. In support of his contention he cited the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil and others, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 10. 

 35. Mr. Rajik-al Jalil, the learned Assistant Attorney General, appearing for the Government, however, submits that the Court of Settlement being a tribunal of facts considered the material points and arrived at correct findings of fact and, as such, this court should not interfere with the decision of the Court of Settlement in its writ jurisdiction. 

 37. Though the entire holding was initially declared as an abandoned property under President's Order 16 of 1972 but on the representation of Khawja Golam Hossain, claiming himself as husband of Mahmuda Khatun, the Government by the memo dated 29-10-1974 (Annexure B) released the entire property from the list of abandoned properties. Relying on the order of release dated 29-10-1974 and mutation dated 31-8-1989 (Annexure B1) of the name of Khawja Golam Hossain in the official record of the Revenue Department the petitioners purchased the entire property by 5 registered kabalas (Annexures C-C 4) from Khawja Golam Hossain and also paid Taka 1,75,000/- to the Government as transfer fee as the disputed property was Khash Mohal holding (Annexure C5). But subsequently, when it was found that since the emergence of Bangladesh the sons and daughters of Mahmuda Khatun are not the residents of Bangladesh the Government in the Ministry of Works after thorough investigation and obtaining opinion of the Ministry of Law in this regard by the memo dated 22-4-1984 (Annexure D) modified the earlier order dated 29-10-1974 by which ¼ th share of Khawja Golam Hossain in the property was deemed to have been released and ¾ th share inherited by the sons and daughters of Mahmuda Khatun remained abandoned. The parties do not also dispute this position. From this position it is presumed that the Government after being satisfied about the status and whereabouts, at the material time of Khawja Golam Hossain, issued memo dated 29-10-1974 and modified the same vide memo dated 22-4-1984. 

 38. It is also undisputed that when it was discovered that Khawja Golam Hossain the vendor of the petitioners was owner only to the extent of ¼ th share of the property and sons and daughters of Mahmuda Khatun inherited the remaining 3/4th share and that portion vested in the Government as abandoned property, the petitioners offered to purchase the remaining 3/4th share from the Government as abandoned property and the Government agreed to sell the entire 3/4th share to the petitioners at Taka 26,34,187/50 and accordingly, informed the petitioner No.1 by memo dated 10-4-1985 (Annexure-E) and the petitioner was asked to pay the price of 3/4th share within 15 days to the Executive Engineer, Abandoned Houses Circle Segunbagicha, Dhaka (Annexure-E to Writ Petition 911 of 2002). From, the said memo dated 10-4-1985 it appears that the Government recognised the present petitioners as owner of ¼th share of the disputed holding. From this position also it is clear that the Government also being satisfied about the genuineness of the transfer by Khawja Golam Hossain to the petitioners issued memo dated 10-4-1985. 

 39. From the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Government in earlier Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985, brought by Atahar Mollah and another (Annexure-F) challenging the decision of the Government to sell the 3/4th share to the petitioners, it is also clear that the Government admitted the release of 1/4th share in favour of Khawja Golam Hossain, vendor of the petitioners, only 3/4th share of the property wasp abandoned. But after release of the ¼th share of Khawja Golam Hossain from the list of abandoned properties and decision of the Govt. to sell the remaining 3/4th share to the petitioners, treating of the entire property including 1/4th share of Khawja Golam Hossain as abandoned property is without any basis. It is also undisputed that even after the said enlistment in ka list, the Abandoned Property. Disposal and Management Board, when dealing with the disposal and management of abandoned properties in the City of Dhaka in its meeting held on 17-12-1992 in pursuance of the earlier decision of the Ministry of Works maintained the earlier decision to sell the 3/4th share only of the disputed property to the petitioners. 

 40. Thus from our above discussion it is clear that the decision of the Government is consistent after proper investigation and after obtaining opinion of the Ministry of Law, regarding release of 1/4th share in favour of Khawja Golam Hossain and decision to sell the remaining 3/4th share in favour of the petitioners who became owners of the released 1/4th share by purchase from Khawja Golam Hossain. That being the position the enlistment of 1/4th share of the holding inherited by Khawja Golam Hossain and sold to the petitioners is not in conformity with the stand taken earlier by the Government in Writ Petition No. 57/1985. 

 41. The petitioners filed application before the Court of Settlement for exclusion of their ¼ th share of the disputed property which they purchased in the year 1982 from Khawja Golam Hossain by registered kabalas. The petitioners, it appears, filed a host of documents and adduced oral evidence in support of their claim and also to disprove the subsequent stand taken by the Government in enlisting the entire holding as Abandoned Property. The Government contested the case without filing any written statement. The Government, however, before the Court of Settlement questioned the identity of Khawja Golam Hossain and genuineness of the documents executed by Khawja Golam Hossain in favour of the petitioners. When the Government after being satisfied about the status of Khawja Golam Hossain and the genuineness of the transfer by him to the petitioners issued memos dated 29-10-1974; 22-4-1984 and 10-4-1985 in our view, the Govt. should not be allowed subsequently to give a go-by to their earlier decision in this regard. 

 43. In the above circumstances we are of the view that the Court of Settlement failed to appreciate the facts involving the jurisdiction and authority of the Government in enlisting the ¼th share of the disputed property in the abandoned list and fell in an error which, obviously, is an illegality in the exercise of jurisdiction. The court of settlement also without considering the material evidence placed before it as discussed above, arrived at a wrong conclusion causing prejudice to the petitioners and this made the impugned judgment liable to be declared void with regard ¼ th share of Khowja Golam Hossain. 

 45. Let us now turn to the question as to whether the petitioners are entitled to get a direction to give effect of the Memo dated 10-4-1985 of the Government and Resolution dated 17-12-1992 of the Abandoned Property Management Board for sale of ¾ th share of the holding to the petitioners. 

 46. We have already found the enlistment of ¼ th share of Khawja Golam Hossain in ka list of abandoned property was without any lawful authority. Thus it appears that the petitioners are the co-sharers to the extent of 1/4th share of the disputed holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka. The Government also by Memo dated 10-4-1985 accepted the petitioners as co-sharers in the disputed holding and accordingly, decided to sell the remaining ¾ th share to them, as we noticed already, and asked the petitioners to deposit Taka 26,34,187/50 within 15 days to the Executive Engineer, Abandoned Houses Circle, Segunbagicha, petition No. 57 of 1985. After disposal of the above writ petition the petitioners by their letter dated 9-12-1991 requested the Secretary of the Ministry (copy of which was endorsed on 10-12-1991 to the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka designated as Chairman of the Abandoned Property Disposal and Management Board) for direction as to under what head the offered money was to be deposited. The said Board by the resolution in its meeting held on 17-12-1992 maintained the earlier decision to sell the property to the petitioners with the said offered price. On receipt of copy of the said resolution under memo dated 6-6-1993, (signed on 25-5-1993) of the Divisional Commissioner (Annexure-F to Writ Petition 1454 of 1994) the petitioners addressed a letter dated 6-6-1993 to the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka seeking instruction as to whom the money was to be deposited as price of 3/4th share of holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka. But no response was made. From the resolution dated 17-12-1992 of the Abandoned Property Board it is clear that the decision to sell the 3/4th share of disputed holding to the petitioners was maintained even after the enlistment of the entire holding in Ka list as Abandoned Property and also after the disposal of Writ Petition 57 of 1985. 

 47. On this factual background Mr. Islam submits that since the Government initially and its delegated authority subsequently made promise to sell the 3/4th share of the disputed holding to the petitioners, they are under legal obligation to make necessary arrangement for transferring the same in favour of the petitioners. 

 48. Mr. Rajik-Al-Jalil, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, tried to argue that since the petitioners did not comply with the direction of the Government contained in Memo dated 10-4-1985 and did not deposit the money within 15 days the petitioners are not entitled to get 3/4th share of the property. 

 49. In reply Mr. Islam submits that since there was a stay order issued on 15-4-1985 in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 and the operation of the Memo dated 10-4-85 was stayed by this court before expiry of 15 days time they could not comply with the direction of the Government in depositing the money as the same was beyond their control. It is further submitted that the present petitioners contested the Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 by filing affidavit in opposition which amply manifests their intention to purchase the 1/4th share of property as they were offered by the Government by Memo dated 10-4-1985 but because of the stay order in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 staying operation of Memo dated 10-4-1985 they could not deposit the money and after disposal of the Writ Petition the petitioners addressed letter to the Ministry and also to the Board as to under how and what head the money is to be deposited but no reply was given. So, in view of our above discussion the argument of the learned Assistant Attorney-General does not stand. 

 50. The learned Assistant Attorney-General further submits that the memo dated 10-4-1985 was merely an administrative decision to sell an abandoned property and did not create any enforceable right in favour of the petitioners and, as such, it is not binding on the Government. 

 51. Mr. Islam, in reply, submits that the Government cannot escape by merely saying that they are not bound by their earlier promise to sell the 3/4th share to the petitioners (contained in Memo dated 10-4-1985) as the Government is under legal obligation towards the petitioners to carry out specific promise and complete the transfer as per Memo dated 10-4-1985 and, as such, the Government is estopped to take any such plea as raised by the learned Assistant Attorney-General. In this connection he has referred to the case of Secretary, Ministry of Industries vs Saleh Ahmed, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 148=1981 BLD (AD) 91 wherein the Appellate Division affirmed the decision of the High Court Division directing the Government to complete the formalities for transfer of a Mill, namely, Mohammadi Calendaring & Printing Mills Ltd. On the factual background that the Government took the decision on agreement to release the Mill to the petitioner but subsequently denied it on the plea of revised decision, the Appellate Division took the view that "the respondents cannot be allowed to act inconsistently and the decision to release the Mill remains binding on them" 

 53. In the circumstances and applying the principle enunciated in the above cited cases we are of the view that the respondent-Government cannot be allowed to act inconsistently with its promise made by memo dated 10-4-1985 which is binding on it. The Government thus cannot be exempted from its liability to carry out its promise given to the petitioners and by the doctrine of promissory estoppel the Government cannot escape from its liability saying that the promise was merely an administrative decision. 

 54. Mr. Islam next submits that the Government in the Ministry of Works by its memo dated 10-4-1985 not only made the promise to sell the 3/4th share of that holding but also by the resolution dated 17-12-1992 of the Abandoned Property Management Board maintained the promise giving rise to a legitimate expectation of the petitioners as the petitioners have completed the legal formalities for such transfer to them but subsequent conduct of respondent is arbitrary, unfair and unreasonable. In such a situation, Mr Islam argued, this Court may protect such expectation of the petitioners, arising from express promise, by directing the authority to act fairly and carry out the promise [even if it is found that the petitioners have no legal right accrued from such promise]. Mr. Islam then referred to the case of Attorney-General of Hong Kong vs Ng Yuen Shiu, reported in (1983) 2 AC 629=(1983) 2 All ER 346. He then cited the case of Rabia Bashri Irene and another vs Bangladesh Binian Corporation, reported in 52 DLR 308 wherein the doctrine of legitimate expectation was applied relying upon the case of Council of Civil Service Union and others vs Minister for the Civil Service decided by House of Lords reported in (1985) AC 374. 

 58. In the above circumstances the memo dated 10-4-1985 and the resolution of the Abandoned Property Management Board dated 17-12-1992 in our view, gave rise to a legitimate expectation of the petitioners to have completed the legal formalities for transferring the property in question to them. Subsequent silence of the Governmental authority amounts to denial of such expectation which is obviously unfair. 

 59. Mr. Halder, learned Advocate for the added respondents, however, submits that the Government has no power or authority to transfer an abandoned property under negotiation as has been done by the memo dated 10-4-1985. He argued that Rule 10(1) of the Abandoned Property (Buildings in the Urban Areas) Rules framed under the Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order 1972, (President's Order 16 of 1972) is a bar to such a transfer and the abandoned property in question cannot be sold in any manner except in the manner as provided in the said Rule. In support of his contention he cited the case of United Commercial Bank Ltd and another vs Rahimafrooz Batteries Ltd and others, reported in 7 BLC (AD) 73. In reply Mr. Islam referred to Articles 4 and 5 of President's Order 16 of 1972 and submits that under Article 4 the Government may dispose of any abandoned property by transfer or otherwise in accordance with the provision of the said President's Order. He, then, argued that the government has adequate power and authority to deal with the abandoned property as was done in the present case by the memo dated 10-4-1985. He further submits that the Rules as framed thereunder should be read with the parent provisions of the President's Order 16 of 1972 as the Rules were framed for the purpose of carrying out the purposes of President's Order 16 of 1972 and the Rule 10(1) should not be read in such a manner where this subordinate legislation overrides the provisions of parent law. Mr. Islam, however, contends that Rule 10, on which Mr. Halder relied, has no manner of application in the present case as the memo dated 10-4-1985 is well covered by Article 5 of President's Order 16 of 1972. 

 "4. On the commencement of this Order, all abandoned properties in Bangladesh shall vest in the Government and shall be administered, controlled, managed and disposed of, by transfer or otherwise, in accordance with the provision of this Order." 

 "5.(1) For the purpose of carrying the provision of this Order into effect and, in particular for the purpose of securing, administration, control, management and disposal by transfer or otherwise, of abandoned property, the Government may take such measures as it considers necessary or expedient and do all acts and incur all expenses necessary or incidental thereto." 

 (2) Without prejudice to generality of . the foregoing provision, the Government may, for the said purpose— 

 62. From the above parent provision of President's Order 16 of 1972 it is clear that the Government is fully authorised to transfer any abandoned property by way of sale and, as such, the provision in clause (c) of Rule 10(1) framed thereunder does not divest the Government of its power to deal with the property in question in the manner as has been done by the memo dated 10-4-1985. Decision in the case of United Commercial Bank Ltd and another vs Rahimafrooz Batteries Ltd and others, reported in 7 BLC (AD) 73, as referred to by Mr. Halder, is regarding the question of retrospection of the new sub-rule 4A of Rule 10. 

 63. Mr. Halder next argued that the present writ petition does not lie as the impugned order dated 10-4-1985 was challenged in writ petition 57 of 1985 by them. He also cited the case of Government of Bangladesh and others vs Sree Luxmi Janardhan Jew Thakur, reported in 10 BLT (AD) 16. The facts of the case cited by Mr. Halder are distinguishable from the facts of the present case and, as such, decision of the cited case is not applicable in the present case. On perusal of the judgment dated 28-5-1991 in Writ Petition No. 57 of 1985 it appears that the Rule was discharged and no finding on the Government Memo dated 10-4-1985 was given. So, question of res judicata, in our view doe's not arise in this writ petition which is very much maintainable. 

 64. For the reasons and discussion above both the Rules Nisi in Writ Petition Nos. 911 of 2002 and 1454 of 1994 are made absolute without any order as to costs. Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order dated 3-1-2002 passed by the Court of Settlement, First Court; Dhaka in Abandoned Property Case No. 29 of 1995 (Annexure-A to the Writ Petition No. 911 of 2002) in respect of holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka so far as it relates to ¼ th share of the petitioners is hereby declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. The respondent-Government is directed to release 1/4th share of the holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka in favour of the petitioners from the ka list of the abandoned property. 

 The respondent-Government is also directed to give effect to the Memo dated 10-4-1985 of the Government of the Ministry of Works (Annexure-A1 to the Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994) and the resolution of the Abandoned Properties Disposal and Management Board, Dhaka as taken in the meeting dated 17-12-1992 and communicated to the petitioner No.1 under its Memo dated 6-3-93 (Annexure-F to the Writ Petition No. 1454 of 1994) and transfer the 3/4th portion of the property being holding No. 58/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka within 60 days from date of receipt of Taka 26,34,187/50 from the petitioners.
